body.statement:
In the finite two-arm sample-and-assign design of Aronow, Green, and Lee, \(N\geq4\), \(n_{\mathrm s}\) units are sampled without replacement, \(m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) sampled units are treated, \(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) are controls, and \(N-n_{\mathrm s}\) are unassigned.  For the difference-in-means estimator, their Equation (2) is
\[
V_N=\frac1{N-1}\left\{
\frac{N-m_{\mathrm t}}{m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{11}^{(N)}(Y)
+\frac{N-(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t})}{n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}}\sigma_{00}^{(N)}(Y)
+2\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)
\right\}.
\]
Given the two finite-population marginal distributions, their Lemma 1 states sharp lower and upper bounds for \(\sigma_{10}^{(N)}(Y)\), and the upper endpoint is attained by the comonotone coupling.  This is an oracle finite-population statement about known marginal distributions, distinct from their subsequent asymptotic analysis of estimated bounds.

source.locator: Section 2, Equation (2), and Section 3, Lemma 1, arXiv:1405.6555v1
source.verbatim_statement: The upper bound is attained if y1 and y0 are comonotonic.
